summary.title: Always do Extra
summary.one_liner: Long-serving programmers spend their leftover time on "Extra" work that is aligned with their project, rather than on more of the same work or on nothing.
takeaways: Divide your work into Normal Work (the base expectations), and then choose what to do with leftover time: More, Extra, or Nothing.
More means taking on additional similar tasks; Extra means exploring something new, such as a library or security practice, that could help the project or your skills.
Extra broadens your skills and employability, and gives you a sense of control over your work.
Extra must be balanced against Normal Work and aligned with the project, and it should be shared openly with the team.
summary.summary: The author argues that the common trait of good, veteran programmers is a habit of doing "Extra" with leftover time, as opposed to "More" (doing more of the same) or "Nothing." Using a worked example of building form screens, they explain that Extra is exploration such as researching a validation library or security practices, which may or may not pay off for the project but adds real value to the developer's skills and sense of agency. The piece includes two rules: Extra must not crowd out Normal Work, and it must be relevant to the current project. It is an opinion essay with no code or technical implementation details.
